title: matra error, schema 2.x
description: One failure as matra reports it: the serde form of `matra::domain::Error` (`kind`, `message`, `details`), and of `matra::domain::DocumentError`, which adds `path`. Python's `Engine.analyze_all` yields the second for a document that failed, and every Python exception matra raises carries the first as `kind`, `str(exc)` and `details`. Read by the same rules as the document schema: ignore fields you do not recognize, treat every string set as open (`kind` and `io_kind` among them), and reject a major you do not know. Branch on `kind`, read values from `details`, and never parse `message`, which is for a person and may change. A detail that does not apply is absent; a key a kind carries keeps appearing in later versions.

kind.description: The stable name of the failure: `model_not_found`, `model_invalid`, `parse_failed`, `input_too_large`, `unsupported_format`, `invalid_input` or `io`. An open set.

message.description: The error's text, for a person. Every dynamic value in it is also in `details`, except on `invalid_input`, whose `details.reason` names the check that failed and whose message adds, for a person, the values that failed it.

details.description: The values a caller acts on, by name: every dynamic value in `message`, except on `invalid_input` (see `message`). The keys depend on `kind`; each value is a string, a whole number or a boolean. One word, one meaning: `reason` is always the stable name of a check that failed, to branch on, and `cause` is always free text for a person.

path.description: On a per-document failure only: the file the document came from, or null for input that never came from disk.
The path where no model was found.

reason.description: The check that failed, a stable snake_case name to branch on, such as `threshold_not_finite`, `embedder_vector_count`, `blocks_malformed`, `config_malformed` or `usage`. The errors reference lists every one. An open set.

cause.description: What went wrong, for a person: the variant's own text.
What went wrong, for a person: the parser's or the reader's own text, or which token or block failed the engine's check and how.

reason.description: Present when the engine's checks on what a parser or a reader returned failed: the check, a stable snake_case name to branch on, such as `head_out_of_range`, `head_cycle` or `block_span_invalid`. The errors reference lists every one. Absent when the parser or the reader reported the failure itself. An open set.

what.description: The gate that fired: `input`, `file_read`, `tfidf`, `textrank`, `rake`, `yake`, `clusters`, `parser_model_download`, `embedding_model_download` or `config_file_read`. An open set.

actual.description: The size measured against the cap.

format.description: The format recognised (`pdf`, `docx`), absent when the bytes are neither UTF-8 text nor a signature matra recognises.

feature.description: The Cargo feature that would read `format`, absent when none does.

io_kind.description: The class of the I/O failure, in snake case: `not_found`, `permission_denied`, `already_exists`, `unsupported`, `invalid_input`, `invalid_data`, `timed_out`, `not_connected`, `connection_refused`, `connection_reset`, `unexpected_eof`, `interrupted`, `not_a_directory`, `is_a_directory`, `storage_full` or `other`. An open set.

path.description: The path the failure concerns, when matra named one.

url.description: The URL of a download that did not arrive.

retryable.description: On a download that did not arrive: whether the same call can be made again as it is and may succeed. Absent elsewhere, which makes no claim either way.

cause.description: The I/O failure's own text, for a person.
